body:
👋 Jules, reporting for duty! I'm here to lend a hand with this pull request.

When you start a review, I'll add a 👀 emoji to each comment to let you know I've read it. I'll focus on feedback directed at me and will do my best to stay out of conversations between you and other bots or reviewers to keep the noise down.

I'll push a commit with your requested changes shortly after. Please note there might be a delay between these steps, but rest assured I'm on the job!

For more direct control, you can switch me to **Reactive Mode**. When this mode is on, I will only act on comments where you specifically mention me with `@jules`. You can find this option in the **Pull Request** section of your [global Jules UI settings](https://jules.google.com/settings). You can always switch back!

New to Jules? Learn more at [jules.google/docs](https://jules.google/docs).

---
*_For security, I will only act on instructions from the user who triggered this task._*

## Second-pass review (post-Jules)

**Verdict: Request changes. Not merge-ready as durable repo documentation.**

> Formal `gh pr review --request-changes` was attempted first (`gh pr review 3 --repo Yuuqq/collection-skill`). The integration token received `403 Resource not accessible by integration (addPullRequestReview)` — same for `gh pr comment` / REST review + issue-comment APIs. Posting the full review here so it is still on the PR.

This PR is a single 60-line `REVIEW.md` (commit `7b464ed`, +60/−0, no code, no tests, no CI). Jules billed it as a “comprehensive” review covering architecture, security, reliability, testing, **performance**, and **documentation**. The document delivers none of the last two, mis-rates most of what it does cover, and never opened `.github/workflows/`, `validate_catalog.py`, `make_digest.py`, `sync_readme_stats.py`, `SKILL.md`, or `references/llm-judging.md`. Merging this as the project’s official review record would teach the next contributor the wrong risks.

I re-read the scripts and workflows against every cited line. Below: finding-by-finding verdict, then the issues Jules missed.

---

### REVIEW.md quality (the actual diff)

A review artifact that wants to live in the repo root needs: reviewed commit SHA + date, scope (what was / was not read), and severity that a maintainer can act on. This file has none of that. It also fights the repo’s own constraints:

- Scripts and `tests/test_validate_catalog.py` are **stdlib-only**. Recommending `tenacity` / `backoff` / `requests` / `httpx` is an architecture regression, not a fix.
- Intro claims performance + documentation coverage; body has **zero** findings in either.
- Several line citations are wrong; several “security” items are Bandit-shaped filler with the caveat already in the same paragraph.

Fix the doc or do not merge it. A stale, inflated review in `REVIEW.md` is worse than no file.

---

### Finding-by-finding

#### HIGH 1 — HTTP error handling / missing tokens — **reject as HIGH; two issues glued together**

Cited lines are in the right neighborhoods (`add_repo.py` 49–67, `discover_repos.py` 177–210 / 293–313), but the write-up mixes (a) urllib retry polish with (b) env-var fallback. Those are not the same bug.

- `GH._get_with_backoff` already retries 403/429/5xx/`URLError` with `Retry-After` and a secondary-limit window. This is not “insufficient.” Suggesting a third-party retry library contradicts stdlib-only.
- Token / `LLM_API_KEY` fallback is **intentional and documented** (`discover_repos.py` docstring, `references/llm-judging.md`, `.last-run.json` so CI does not lie about “LLM-judged”). Calling a designed fallback “silent failure” without reading that machinery is sloppy.
- The *real* operational gap is narrower and lives in CI, which this review never opened: `.github/workflows/discover.yml` sets `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}` and still `git commit` + `git push` after a heuristic fallback. **Fail-closed in the workflow when `GH_PAT` is empty** is a fair MEDIUM. It is not a urllib problem.

#### HIGH 2 — Input validation / Markdown sanitization — **reject as HIGH; citation is wrong**

`add_repo.py` 81–105 is `repo_to_entry`’s return dict and `PRESERVED_FIELDS`, **not** argparse. Notes / extra-tags are at 109–121.

This is a **local curator CLI**, not a public input surface. JSON dump already escapes control characters. `build_catalog_md.py` interpolates description/notes/tags without a `_cell()`-style escape (unlike `make_digest.py`, which Jules also did not read). Worst case is a broken generated `.md` in-repo, not XSS. Cap at **LOW**, and cite the right lines.

Also missed the actual `add_repo.py` correctness bug on the same path (see below).

#### MEDIUM 1 — Test coverage gaps — **keep, but incomplete**

Correct that only `validate_catalog.py` is tested. Incomplete:

- There is **no PR/CI job that even runs those tests**. `.github/workflows/` has `discover.yml` + `weekly-digest.yml` only. `repo-schema.md` says “CI runs the validator as a gate” — that gate is inside the weekly discover job, not on pull requests. This PR itself is evidence: no checks.
- Highest-value untested units are `parse_keywords`, `_parse_judge_array`, `passes_filter` / `COLLECTION_SIGNALS`, and `add_repo` merge/preserve — not a vague “mock the GitHub API.”

#### MEDIUM 2 — Insecure randomness — **drop or LOW / noise**

Line 292 is `random.choice(self.api_keys)` for key-pool load balancing. Jules already admits it is not crypto. `secrets.choice` does not change the threat model. This is a Bandit hit, not a finding. Do not ship it as MEDIUM in a repo-root review.

#### MEDIUM 3 — “File path traversal” via `urlopen` — **misnamed, overrated**

This is unexpected-scheme / SSRF folklore, not path traversal. GitHub URLs are hardcoded `https://api.github.com`. The one user-influenced URL is `LLM_BASE_URL` (env/CLI) — operator-controlled, not attacker-controlled. Switching to `requests`/`httpx` is again a dependency grab. If you want a real hardening note: reject non-`https` schemes on `LLM_BASE_URL`. That is LOW.

#### MEDIUM 4 — “Potential command injection” — **not a finding**

`subprocess.run(["gh", "auth", "token"], ...)` is argv, `shell=False`, constants only. “Risky if someone later interpolates user input” is a lecture. Delete it.

Current process is fine. The **actual** shell-injection surface is in `discover.yml` (missed; below).

#### LOW 1 — Duplication — **fair**

Token lookup + urllib wrappers are copy-pasted. A tiny `scripts/http_gh.py` (still stdlib) is enough. Do not pull in `requests` to “dedupe.”

#### LOW 2 — Hardcoded paths — **factually wrong**

Paths are `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "references"/...`. That is why the scripts **do** run from an arbitrary cwd. `discover_repos.py` already has `--catalog`; `build_catalog_md.py` has `--json`/`--out`; `validate_catalog.py` has `--json`. Only `add_repo.py` hardcodes the catalog path. Rewrite or delete.

#### LOW 3 — No lint CI — **fair, secondary**

Yes, no `flake8`/`black`/`bandit` job. Running the **existing** unittest suite on PRs matters more than adding Bandit so it can flag `random.choice` again.

---

### What Jules missed (this is the actual review of the codebase)

These are in the tree Jules claimed to have reviewed. None appear in `REVIEW.md`.

1. **Actions script injection — MEDIUM** (`.github/workflows/discover.yml` ~41–48)

   ```yaml
   if [ -n "${{ github.event.inputs.categories }}" ]; then
     ARGS="$ARGS --categories ${{ github.event.inputs.categories }}"
   fi
   python scripts/discover_repos.py $ARGS
   ```

   `workflow_dispatch` input is spliced into a `run:` script *before* the shell parses it. `$(...)`, backticks, and quotes in `categories` execute as shell. Write access is required to dispatch, so this is not internet-RCE — it is still the textbook GHA injection footgun and the first thing a security pass should have cited. Fix: env var + quoted expansion, or validate against the five category enums in the workflow before exec.

2. **Long-lived PAT used as `GITHUB_TOKEN` + embedded in push URL — MEDIUM** (`discover.yml` 36, 78)

   Scheduled job overwrites default-branch catalog with `secrets.GH_PAT`, then `git push "https://${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}@github.com/..."`. A user PAT is over-scoped vs `contents: write` `GITHUB_TOKEN`, lives forever, and does not expire with the job. Actions will mask the secret *if* it is set; empty PAT still produces a broken remote and a heuristic catalog commit attempt. Prefer `GITHUB_TOKEN` + `contents: write` (already declared) or a fine-scoped bot token via `git remote set-url` / `gh auth setup-git`, never `https://$PAT@`.

3. **`COLLECTION_SIGNALS` is so broad it disables pruning — MEDIUM / correctness** (`discover_repos.py` 473–479, 640–646)

   Signals include `数据`, `sdk`, `browser`, `parser`, `fetch`. Almost any Chinese-language repo and a huge fraction of GitHub will match. Combined with default `--rescan` of the **entire** catalog, the LLM exclude path is mostly dead. This is the core quality risk of weekly discovery. Jules’s “LLM judge might fail unnoticed” note is downstream of this.

4. **`references/llm-judging.md` documents code that does not exist — MEDIUM / docs-code drift**

   Section “Deterministic `agent-skill` cleanup” claims unprotected `agent-skill` entries without a collection signal are pruned. `discover_repos.py` has `_is_protected` + `_has_collection_signal` as *keep* guards only. There is no agent-skill sweep. The reference file is the contract for the weekly job; it is currently lying. A “comprehensive” review that never opened it is incomplete.

5. **`add_repo.py` `--extra-tags` / `--platform` are no-ops on update — MEDIUM / correctness** (162–189)

   Tags are built on `entry`, then `PRESERVED_FIELDS` copies existing `tags` over them. CLI overrides exist for notes/favorite/use_cases/caveats, **not** tags. CONTRIBUTING tells people to use this script to add tools. That path is broken for the chinese-social tag Jules’s own HIGH 2 was worrying about.

6. **`add_repo.py` docstring lies** (lines 9–12)

   Usage string is syntactically broken (`[--notes "..." [--favorite]`). Text says omitting `--category` prompts the user; `main()` `sys.exit`s. Small, but this is the contributor entrypoint.

7. **No test job on PRs — MEDIUM**

   18 unittests exist (`repo-schema.md` even advertises `python -m unittest discover -s tests`). No workflow runs them. Lint-envy without this is backwards.

8. **Untrusted GitHub copy → LLM → generated Markdown** (`discover_repos.py` `judge()` + `build_catalog_md.py` `_render_card`)

   Public repo descriptions/topics go into the judge prompt; model `use_cases` are written back and rendered raw. Prompt-injection / catalog-MD injection is a real (low-urgency) content-trust issue. `make_digest.py` already has `_cell()`; the catalog renderer does not. This is a better sanitization finding than “user typed `--notes` locally.”

---

### Security / regressions / merge readiness

| Axis | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Correctness of REVIEW.md | Multiple wrong citations, one inverted path claim, two HIGH findings that are not HIGH |
| Security value | Bandit false positives in; Actions injection + PAT-in-URL + signal-list bypass out |
| Regressions if merged | No runtime regression (docs-only). Process regression: this file becomes the “known issues” list and will freeze bad priorities |
| REVIEW.md quality | Fail. Incomplete scope, inflated severity, contradicts stdlib-only, no pin to a commit |
| Merge | **Do not merge as-is** |

**What would make this mergeable**

- Pin `Reviewed: 7e19170` (or whatever tree was actually read) and list files in / out of scope.
- Demote HIGH 1 → optional CI fail-closed note; demote HIGH 2 → LOW; delete MEDIUM 2 and MEDIUM 4; fix LOW 2.
- Add the missed items above, or explicitly say workflows were not reviewed.
- Do not recommend new PyPI deps.
- Better: keep this review on the PR and **do not** land a `REVIEW.md` in the skill repo at all. This tree is a catalog + agent skill, not a place for a one-shot audit memo.

I am not approving a document that would become the canonical risk register while missing the weekly job that writes the catalog.
